title: Kava extract for treating anxiety
citationText: Pittler MH, Ernst E. Kava extract for treating anxiety. Cochrane Database Syst Rev. 2003;(1):CD003383.
notes: Baseline provenance recovery for normalized enrichment. Exact legacy sourceId preserved; the review is dated and should not be treated as a freshness signal for new claims.

title: Kava for the treatment of generalized anxiety disorder RCT: analysis of adverse reactions, liver function, addiction, and sexual effects
citationText: Sarris J, et al. Kava for the treatment of generalized anxiety disorder RCT: analysis of adverse reactions, liver function, addiction, and sexual effects. Phytother Res. 2013;27(11):1723-1728.
notes: Six-week double-blind randomized trial in 75 adults with generalized anxiety disorder using Kava tablets providing 120 mg kavalactones/day, titrated in nonresponders to 240 mg/day. No significant group differences in liver function tests and no significant adverse reactions attributable to Kava were reported. This does not establish long-term safety, exclude rare hepatotoxicity, or establish safety in pre-existing liver disease.

title: EPIDIOLEX (cannabidiol) oral solution — 2021 prescribing information
citationText: U.S. Food and Drug Administration. EPIDIOLEX (cannabidiol) oral solution prescribing information. 2021 labeling revision.
notes: Inactive historical provenance only. Retained so deprecated audit records remain traceable; it must not support current publishable claims because newer EPIDIOLEX labeling is available.

title: EPIDIOLEX (cannabidiol) oral solution — prescribing information
citationText: U.S. Food and Drug Administration. EPIDIOLEX (cannabidiol) oral solution prescribing information. Revised May 2026.
notes: Current labeling revised 05/2026. Sections 7.2 and 7.4 support CYP2C19-substrate interaction and additive CNS-depressant sedation cautions for prescription cannabidiol.

title: Anti-inflammatory effects of luteolin: A review of in vitro, in vivo, and in silico studies
citationText: Aziz N, Kim MY, Cho JY. Anti-inflammatory effects of luteolin: A review of in vitro, in vivo, and in silico studies. J Ethnopharmacol. 2018;225:342-358.
notes: Baseline provenance recovery. Taxonomized as preclinical-mechanistic because the review is dominated by in-vitro, in-vivo, and in-silico evidence; it must not be counted as direct human efficacy evidence.

title: Therapeutic efficacy and safety of chamomile for state anxiety, generalized anxiety disorder, insomnia, and sleep quality: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials and quasi-randomized trials
citationText: Hieu TH, et al. Therapeutic efficacy and safety of chamomile for state anxiety, generalized anxiety disorder, insomnia, and sleep quality: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Phytother Res. 2019;33(6):1604-1615.
notes: Baseline provenance recovery for normalized enrichment. Exact legacy sourceId preserved.

title: An investigation into the stress-relieving and pharmacological actions of an ashwagandha (Withania somnifera) extract: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study
citationText: Lopresti AL, Smith SJ, Malvi H, Kodgule R. An investigation into the stress-relieving and pharmacological actions of an ashwagandha extract: a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study. Medicine (Baltimore). 2019;98(37):e17186.
notes: Baseline provenance recovery. Small 60-day Shoden trial in stressed healthy adults. The article reports no adverse events; acknowledgements state Arjuna Natural Ltd funded the project and supplied the extract, so null safety findings require sponsorship and sample-size context.

title: The Effectiveness and Safety of Cannabidiol in Non-seizure-related Indications: A Systematic Review of Published Randomized Clinical Trials
citationText: Tang Y, Tonkovich KL, Rudisill TM. The Effectiveness and Safety of Cannabidiol in Non-seizure-related Indications: A Systematic Review of Published Randomized Clinical Trials. Pharmaceut Med. 2022;36(6):353-385.
notes: Systematic review of 58 randomized studies outside seizure disorders. It found highly variable effectiveness, mostly small studies, and called for larger diverse samples and clearer dosing guidance; authors reported no relevant competing interests.

title: Cannabidiol and Liver Enzyme Level Elevations in Healthy Adults: A Randomized Clinical Trial
citationText: Florian J, et al. Cannabidiol and Liver Enzyme Level Elevations in Healthy Adults: A Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA Intern Med. 2025;185(9):1070-1078.
notes: Baseline provenance recovery for normalized enrichment. FDA-led randomized trial in healthy adults; exact legacy sourceId preserved.

title: Beauty of the beast: anticholinergic tropane alkaloids in therapeutics
citationText: Shim KH, Kang MJ, Sharma N, An SSA. Beauty of the beast: anticholinergic tropane alkaloids in therapeutics. Nat Prod Bioprospect. 2022;12(1):33.
notes: Narrative review of tropane-alkaloid pharmacology. Mandragora officinarum is named as a tropane source, which is the mandrake entity link. PubMed types it Journal Article + Review, so it is classed preclinical-mechanistic here. That DOWNGRADES the submission-authored human-clinical class: this record must not back a human-clinical claim.

title: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis on the Survival of Cancer Patients Treated with a Fermented Viscum album L. Extract (Iscador): An Update of Findings
citationText: Ostermann T, Appelbaum S, Poier D, Boehm K, Raak C, Bussing A. Complement Med Res. 2020;27(4):260-271.
notes: Viscum album is mistletoe, so the entity link is exact. HIGH-STAKES: admission makes this citable, it does NOT promote a mistletoe cancer-survival efficacy claim. Iscador survival meta-analyses are a contested, industry-adjacent literature, hence tier-c. Any supported_use or efficacy_signal built on this source needs separate human editorial adjudication, enforced by editorialAdjudication rather than by this note.

editorialAdjudication.reason: Cancer-survival efficacy from a contested, industry-adjacent Iscador literature is a YMYL editorial decision. Admitting the source made it citable; it does not authorize a mistletoe survival efficacy claim.

title: Microclimatic variation in UV perception and related disparity in tropane and quinolizidine alkaloid composition of Atropa acuminata, Lupinus polyphyllus and Hyoscyamus niger
citationText: Jan S, Kamili AN, Parray JA, Bedi YS, Ahmad P. J Photochem Photobiol B. 2016;161:230-235.
notes: Plant-chemistry study. Hyoscyamus niger is henbane, so the entity link is exact. Alkaloid-composition variation only; carries no human efficacy or safety evidence.

title: A new species of Periglandula symbiotic with the morning glory Ipomoea tricolor
notes: Fungal taxonomy and genomics establishing the ergot-alkaloid-producing symbiont of Ipomoea tricolor. Entity link exact. Contains no human evidence of any kind.

title: Ergot Alkaloids and their Hallucinogenic Potential in Morning Glories
citationText: Steiner U, Leistner E. Planta Med. 2018;84(11):751-758.
notes: Phytochemistry review of ergot alkaloids in Convolvulaceae. Rivea corymbosa is a morning glory, which gives the entity link. Hallucinogenic potential here is a chemical characterisation, not a clinical or dosing claim.

title: Jatropodagines A and B: Lathyrane Diterpenoid Dimers from Jatropha podagrica, Inducing Paraptosis-Like Cell Death
citationText: Zhao Q, Zhang W, Zhang J, Chen M, Wang C, Zhang Y. Org Lett. 2026;28:4151-4156.
notes: Natural-product isolation with in-vitro cell-death activity. Entity link exact to Jatropha podagrica. In-vitro cytotoxicity is not a therapeutic or safety claim.

title: Analysis of bioactive composites and antiviral activity of Iresine herbstii extracts against Newcastle disease virus
citationText: Andleeb R, Ashraf A, Muzammil S, et al. Saudi J Biol Sci. 2019;27(1):335-340.
notes: Phytochemical screening plus antiviral testing in embryonated chicken eggs against an avian pathogen. Entity link exact to Iresine herbstii. Veterinary and in-ovo only; nothing here transfers to human antiviral use.

title: Chemo-taxonomic and biological potential of highly therapeutic plant Pedicularis groenlandica Retz. using multiple microscopic techniques
citationText: Hameed A, Zafar M, Ahmad M, Sultana S, Bahadur S, Anjum F. Microsc Res Tech. 2021;84(12):2890-2905.
notes: Microscopy and chemotaxonomy. Entity link exact to Pedicularis groenlandica. The word therapeutic in the title is author framing and is not clinical evidence.

title: Cannabidiol in Developmental Epilepsy: Organoid-Guided Precision Medicine Across Critical Neurodevelopmental Windows
citationText: Joo J, Yang WS, Koh HJ. Int J Mol Sci. 2026;27(6):2899.
notes: Narrative review centred on brain-organoid models. PubMed types it Journal Article + Review. It discusses approved paediatric CBD indications, but this record must not be used to back a human-clinical CBD claim; that regulatory evidence has its own sources.
